meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 2 (Multi-Select): Architecture & Components
meta.format: multi_select: questions use the 'answers' array (multiple correct options). Some include an 'All of the above' option that is only correct when every other option is.

questions.question: Which statements about MCP participants are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The host is the AI application coordinating one or multiple MCP clients
Each MCP client maintains a dedicated connection to exactly one server
A remote Streamable HTTP server typically serves many clients
Local STDIO servers typically serve many clients simultaneously
The term 'MCP server' changes meaning depending on where the program runs

questions.explanation: Host→many clients, client↔one server; remote servers serve many clients while local STDIO servers typically serve a single client. 'MCP server' refers to the program serving context regardless of where it runs.

questions.question: Which responsibilities belong to the DATA layer (as opposed to the transport layer)? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Defining the JSON-RPC 2.0 message structure and semantics
Core primitives such as tools, resources, and prompts
Connection establishment and message framing
Discovery of protocol versions and capabilities
Transport-specific authorization

questions.explanation: The data layer (inner) covers JSON-RPC semantics, primitives, discovery, and notifications; the transport layer (outer) handles connections, framing, and transport-level authorization.

questions.question: Under the 2026-07-28 stateless model, which fields belong in every request's _meta? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion (required)
io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities (required)
io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo (should be included unless configured not to)
io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo (required on requests)
Mcp-Session-Id (required on requests)

questions.explanation: Requests must carry protocolVersion and clientCapabilities, and clients should include clientInfo. serverInfo appears in the server's RESULT _meta, and Mcp-Session-Id was removed entirely.

questions.question: Which statements about 2026-07-28 change notifications are true? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: They are opt-in via a subscriptions/listen request naming the wanted notification types
The server acknowledges with notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged before other notifications on that subscription
Every notification on the stream carries io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId in _meta
Delivery is guaranteed exactly-once across reconnects
Request-scoped notifications like notifications/progress also travel on the subscriptions/listen stream

questions.explanation: Notifications are opt-in, acknowledged first, and tagged with the subscription ID (the listen request's JSON-RPC id). Delivery is best-effort (clients should also poll), and request-scoped notifications flow on the originating request's response stream instead.

questions.question: Which fields does a server/discover result contain? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: supportedVersions — the protocol revisions the server speaks
capabilities — including any supported extensions
serverInfo — the server's identity
ttlMs and cacheScope — how long and where the discovery result may be cached
All of the above

questions.explanation: All four are part of the mandatory server/discover response in 2026-07-28 — here 'All of the above' is genuinely correct, so both the individual letters and E count.

questions.question: Which notification types can a client opt into via subscriptions/listen? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: toolsListChanged
promptsListChanged
resourcesListChanged
resourceSubscriptions (per-resource updates)
progressUpdates

questions.explanation: The four opt-in types are the list-changed trio plus resourceSubscriptions. Progress is request-scoped and flows on the originating request's response stream, never on subscriptions/listen.

questions.question: Under the stateless 2026-07-28 model, which statements are true? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Every request carries io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion in _meta
Every request carries io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities in _meta
Clients SHOULD include io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo on each request
Any server instance behind a load balancer can answer any request
All of the above

questions.explanation: All four hold — self-contained requests are exactly what enables round-robin load balancing and serverless deployment. 'All of the above' is correct here.

questions.question: Which statements about the two transports are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: stdio: the client launches the server as a subprocess and speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout
stdio: stderr is the safe channel for logging
Streamable HTTP: client messages travel as HTTP POST, optionally answered with an SSE stream
Streamable HTTP: a broken SSE stream can be resumed with Last-Event-ID
All of the above

questions.explanation: SSE resumability was removed in 2026-07-28 — a broken stream loses the in-flight request, which the client re-issues with a new ID. That sinks D and the all-of-the-above option.
